source.title: Disentangling the Linguistic Competence of Privacy-Preserving BERT
source.authors: Stefan Arnold; Nils Kemmerzell; Annika Schreiner

record.tranche_reason: The study measures representational similarity between BERT models trained with and without text-to-text privacy perturbation. It finds substantially reduced, but not absent, similarity; this refines the claim toward partial alignment in this setting. It does not test a scale trend.
record.gate_note: The RSA measurements bear on representational alignment. Perplexity, linguistic probing, and attention-clustering findings are not rows because they do not measure the claim's cross-model representational alignment. Values in Figure 2 are included only where the text states them explicitly.
record.test_reason: The study is about privacy perturbation, not convergence. It does report one direct convergence result: an RSA bound of 0.9051 between same-architecture BERT models trained from different initializations. That bears on V3 in a new setting (from-scratch BERT, RSA). The private-vs-public comparison (0.7601) measures how corrupting the training text changes representations. It is confounded with a large capability loss (perplexity 61.45 vs 6.82), so it is not a clean test of V1 or V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that private BERT keeps the hierarchical order of linguistic formalisms. In their account the overall similarity loss reflects failure to capture context, while lexical and localized properties are preserved. They caution that their conclusions rest largely on probing.
record.recipe_differences: Uses RSA on cosine-distance matrices with Spearman correlation to compare privacy modalities; it does not reproduce the original claim's scale or cross-modal tests.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported RSA varies by layer: it starts at 0.9007 for lexical representations and declines across contextual layers to 0.6784. No alternative metric or input-set comparison is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: Training BERT on DP-perturbed text (ε=10) lowers RSA with the clean-text model to 0.7601, versus 0.9051 across seeds. Similarity falls from 0.9007 at the lexical layer to 0.6784 in contextual layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Corrupting or perturbing training data lowers representational similarity to a clean-trained model, most strongly in deeper, contextual layers; the effect is confounded with lower model capability.

record.problems: Only one BERT architecture and one privacy-modality comparison are tested; the model size is not stated. The RSA result uses one metric setup and a 5,000-sentence WikiText sample, with no uncertainty reported. The same-initialization reference is described as an empirical bound, but its details are not stated here.
record.rows_left_out: No additional RSA measurements with explicit numeric values are stated in the text. Figure 2 shows other layer-wise values, but they are not numerically described in the prose.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep and no cross-architecture or cross-objective comparison.
No vision or paired image-caption data.
Does not test unit-level or basis-level non-correspondence, or shared features and subspaces specifically; only overall RSA geometry is reported.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation test.
No interpretable feature or circuit comparison.
One metric setup (cosine + Spearman RSA) and one input set; no comparison across metrics or inputs.
No test of plateau or of shared data or objectives as the cause of alignment. The perturbation comparison is confounded with capability loss.

missing.what: Layer-wise RSA values for the seed-only baseline. The text says these stay 'consistently high RSA values across all layers' but gives them only in Figure 2.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V7 limits_scope label is dropped. r1–r3 compare a corrupted-data model with a clean one, not independently trained models converging. The 0.76 vs 0.905 gap mixes a data difference with a capability difference, so it cannot speak to V7's causal or plateau claims. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep; no test of alignment increasing with scale across independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data.
No paired image-caption data or vision-language models.
The study gives an empirical similarity bound for BERT models with different initializations but does not measure shared features or subspaces across seeds.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test.
No test of recurring interpretable features or circuits.
Uses one similarity setup and one sentence sample; it does not compare similarity metrics, metric settings, or input distributions.

Does not test whether alignment plateaus or whether shared data or objectives explain alignment. Its comparison changes the privacy modality while retaining the general training setup; it does not isolate causes of similarity.

rows.subject: BERT trained on Wikipedia with ε = 10 vs. BERT trained on Wikipedia with ε = ∞
rows.operation_detail: Compared representational dissimilarity structures using RSA; cosine distance within each model and Spearman correlation across models.

conditions.value: text-to-text privatization at ε = 10 versus no privacy bound at ε = ∞

rows.note: The authors describe this as a substantial departure between internal representations. The compared models share architecture and training setup apart from privacy modality.
rows.check: Measures the effect of DP-perturbed training text on representations of the same architecture. The models differ in data corruption and also in capability (perplexity 61.45 vs 6.82), so no version is cleanly tested. V7 concerns causes of convergence across independent models, not whether corruption lowers similarity. Moved to fits_no_version.

tranche.reason: The privacy study reports its own cross-initialization BERT similarity measurement, providing a result on V3 in this setting.

source_check.notes: The 0.9051 value is an empirical reference bound that also measures cross-initialization similarity. Seed count, uncertainty, and the precise averaging procedure are not stated; it establishes relational similarity rather than individual feature correspondence.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: BERT models trained on Wikipedia with ε = 10 versus ε = ∞, evaluated on 5,000 WikiText sentences
reader_labels.reason: Similarity is substantial but below the study's 0.9051 same-architecture/different-initialization reference, and declines from 0.9007 at the lexical layer to 0.6784 across contextual layers (r1–r3). This supports only partial alignment in the tested setting; it does not establish why the models align or whether alignment plateaus.
